en: Since ya boil the chicken 'til the mizutaki broth gets real milky, the soup is chock full a' collagen.
It's even lighter than eatin' chicken meat. I highly recommend it.
Ooh, I'll hafta get some soon, then!
(Mizutaki's good for the skin? Maybe I could talk about that at the cabaret club.)
Apparently there's some special vendin' machine in the area, only one of its kind in the whole dang country. Y'should check it out if ya wanna get some juice in ya.
That a fact? What's it sell?
Huh. Y'know, I'm not too sure.
Then what difference does it make!? I'll just get something from 'round here. I'm thirstier than a hog in a desert!
C'mon! Let's just look a bit harder!
(A one-of-a-kind vending machine? Interesting. Maybe I could talk about that at the cabaret club.)
Next year's my coming-of-age ceremony, so my mom went and got me a Hakata textile sash!
No way! Ain't that real expensive?
Well, it's a once-in-a-lifetime event, after all. Gotta have the right duds to celebrate.
I hear they make wedding dresses outta that stuff too! I'd sure love to try one on sometime.
(Hakata textiles are popular with women. Maybe I could talk about that at the cabaret club.)
Lately I've been eating curry soup every morning.
Why's that? Did you make too much of it?
No. Actually, the spices in curry warm your body up and promote better metabolism.
If you're dieting, it's better to eat it in the morning when you're just starting to move your body, instead of before going to bed.
No way. You can go on a diet with curry?
Oh yes. Certain spices even have anti-aging properties, while others help regulate your digestive tract. So they're good even if you're not dieting!
Wow! And curry soup's not heavy, so I bet it's easy to eat in the morning. I'll have to give it a try sometime.
(A curry soup breakfast diet, huh? I could talk about that at the cabaret club.)
Hey man, let's go get some uni!
Now's no good. Uni isn't in season until July.
Season? Uni has a season?
Sure. Different species of uni are harvested at different times throughout the year.
The best of the best is bafun uni, which is mainly caught in July.

Wow, you sure know a lot about this stuff!
But I don't want to wait until July...
(Uni is in season in July, huh? Sounds like somethin' to mention at the cabaret club.)
I've been going to bed with my hot water bottle every night lately.
Isn't it a pain to fill those up with hot water yourself? You should be fine as long as you turn up your heater.
But the newest ones have super cute covers! I have this fluffy one, and it's so adorable I want to cuddle right up with it!
Then why not get a body pillow instead?
No need! The bottles come in lots of shapes, so you can wrap it around your neck or hang it on your shoulder. There's one you wear like shoes too.
Wow! My shoulders have been killing me lately. I should give one of those a try!
(Hot water bottles for cold days, huh? Maybe I could talk about that at the cabaret club.)
New Year's will finally be here soon. I'm looking forward to the traditional meal.
I guess if yer in here, there's not much else to look forward to.
By the way, did you know that here in Hokkaido they eat the New Year's meal on New Year's Eve?
What? They don't eat it on New Year's Day?
Nah. My cellmate's from Hokkaido, and that's what he said. I'm guessing that's not gonna be the case in prison, though.
(New Year's meals in Hokkaido. Once I get outta here, that'd be a conversation topic.)
I hear that karaage specialty shops are all the rage these days.
Don't I know it. You're talkin' about all-you-can-eat karaage places, yeah?
Then did ya know that Oita prefecture consumes the largest amount o' chicken in the country? And Oita's karaage is finger lickin' delish.
Really? How's it different from regular karaage?
Oita style karaage has strong flavorin' based on a spicy marinade that's made with soy sauce and salt.
The marinade also has garlic and ginger too, so ya don't get bored of its taste at an all-you-can-eat joint!
Whoaaa, that sounds tasty! Next time we go out drinkin', let's hit a place like that up!
(Oita style karaage, huh? I bet I could talk about that at the cabaret club.)
I can't do okonomiyaki 'cause it makes me fat. You know I'm dietin', don't ya?
Nah, okonomiyaki's great for a diet. Wheat flour is low in fat and packed with protein, vitamins, and minerals!
But I ain't gonna eat just wheat flour.
Cabbage is nutritious and low-calorie too, and pork's got lotsa vitamin B1. And since the sauce doesn't have oil, it's low in calories too.
No way! It's gotta be loaded with calories!
Only if ya use fatty cuts of meat and mayo. Yakisoba, cheese, and mochi are all high in calories.
But if ya switch out those ingredients, you can have a low-calorie, healthy meal. It's great food for dieters.
Wow, I'da never expected that! If that's true, I guess maybe I can have some!
(An okonomiyaki diet, huh? I could talk about that at the cabaret club.)
Hey there, sonny. You eat miso, I take it?
Miso? Of course.
Miso's good for health and beauty, y'know. The stuff's packed with all sortsa nutrients, like proteins and minerals.
I never knew that. Just tastes good to me.
Oh, yes! It's good for the stomach and prevents cancer, high blood pressure, stroke, diabetes, a fatty liver, aging, cholesterol, and even aids metabolism.
They say a bowl of miso a day keeps the doctor away. That's how good it is for your health.
(Miso's got health and beauty benefits, huh? Sounds like a good topic to bring up at the cabaret club.)
There's not much meat on tebasaki, is there? I feel like I'm losing out, compared to karaage.
Nah, you've got it backwards! The skin of tebasaki chicken wings has the highest amount of collagen outta all the other parts of a chicken.
They're also loaded with vitamin A, which has anti-aging properties and strengthens your bones and joints.
That's why they're perfect for girls who don't eat all that much.
Well, I'll be! Guess I should get me some tebasaki, then!
(Tebasaki are packed with collagen. I should talk about that at the cabaret club.)
Do you have plans for the Christmas holiday? I'm taking a trip to Maui, myself.
You don't say. I'm heading to do some skiing in Aspen, Colorado.
Why would you go skiing when it's already so cold? Isn't it better to go on a ski trip to Australia when it's summer here?
This is how the rich and famous in LA do it. The West Coast is warm year-round, so they go to snowy climates in order to enjoy a white Christmas.
Is that so? I guess I'm never going to join the ranks of the rich and famous if I just go to Hawaii.
(Christmas done like the celebs in L.A., huh? I should talk about that at the cabaret club.)
Piping hot takoyaki's the best on a cold day!
Oh, no. Takoyaki's great to eat during the hot summer months, too.
Oh wow, really?
Out in Kansai, we have Hangesho eleven days after the summer solstice. We have a tradition of eating octopus around that time.
See, octopus is rich in taurine and zinc, which helps you recover from exhaustion. So, it's great for preventing summer heat fatigue.
Whoa, I had no idea it was such a healthy food!
Hangesho falls on July 2nd, so it's been designated as Octopus Day. I make sure to eat some takoyaki on that day every year.
(Octopus is good for fighting exhaustion, huh? Maybe I'll talk about it at the cabaret club.)
Welcome! What are you in the mood for today, sir?
(I don't feel like hanging out alone tonight.)
I'm good for now. I'll come back some other time.
We hope you'll come by again soon.
(I have work to do. I should come back when I have more free time.)
Could you find me a cabaret club?
A cabaret club? Excellent choice. In that case, I highly recommend La Seine.
Could you tell me a bit more about it?
La Seine is on Nagasu Boulevard. It's a bit cozier than a famous club like Olivier, but it's also nowhere near as expensive.
Great, lead the way.
Sir, your friend seems to be waiting on you.
Ah, right. Sorry about that. I'll come back later.
I'll be waiting for you!
Very well, sir. Please give me one moment while I check in with the club.
Hello? This is Kato from Nagasu Night Navi.
I have a gentleman here who wishes to visit your establishment.
Is now a good time? All right, thank you very much.
All set, sir. If you'll please follow me.
(Damn, I don't have the money.)
Hold it. I'll have to come back later.
We hope you'll come again!
I think I'll pass for now.
Is there anything you'd like to know more about?
Since your time in the club is limited, do your best to make yourself as appealing as you can to the hostess in question.
If all you do is make her talk, she's likely to get bored of you quite quickly.
You'd be better off visiting various establishments around town, to pick up on local gossip. That way you'll have plenty of things to talk about.
That's not a bad idea. Well-traveled men definitely have a lot more conversational savvy.
Indeed. And if talking isn't doing the trick, you could always try spending more money.
Like ordering more expensive liquor?
Precisely. You could also give the lady presents to increase her favor. Oh, and putting in a little extra effort into how you dress never hurts either.
If you're willing to spend the money, you're likely to get a return on your investment.
Guys who are cheap aren't well-liked, huh?
Not usually, no. It is important to be able to get a hostess the very best drink you can.
Spending big amounts of cash can win a girl over in a surprisingly short period of time, so if you're in a hurry, try saving up some money.
So if you're a good conversationalist, you don't need to spend as much money, right?
Correct. If you don't want to spend a great deal of money, it is advisable to find other ways to get the lady to like you.
Thanks. I think I get it now.
Oh, right! There's one more important thing I forgot to mention.
If things are going really well, it can be a good idea to take your leave.
If you keep prattling on after that, you risk killing the mood and undoing all the hard work you did.
That's good to keep in mind.
Lastly, before you leave, be sure to ask her if she'd like to go out with you on a date later.
Taking a hostess on a date can further increase her fondness for you, especially if you are able to work the right magic.
I see. You've been very helpful. Thanks.
Do you have any other questions?
You can invite hostesses out to join you on dates. During these you can grab a bite to eat, go shopping, or play games together.
Taking them out on dates will increase their affection towards you, so you've got nothing to lose by asking them out when you visit the club.
But just because you ask her out, it doesn't necessarily mean she'll say yes.
Correct. Whether she takes you up on your offer or not depends largely on her mood.
If you're not good enough friends with her, she'll most likely reject your proposal.
If that's the case, then try to improve her mood. It's important for her to have a good time as well.
Also, if you show up at the club and ask her out right away, you're probably not going to get a very positive response either.
I see. The timing is important, then.
Oh, yes. But if she turns you down, don't give up. If you keep on asking, she may eventually give in and say yes.
I'll keep that in mind.
Oh, I wouldn't possibly know anything about that...
Oh. Too bad.
No, wait, I have something! Once you've talked your hostess up as much as you can, you normally wouldn't need to order anything else for the remainder of your time.
However, if you order something anyway, she might treat you to a... different sort of hospitality.
A different sort of hospitality? Meaning what, exactly?
You knooow, things like hand-feeding you pieces of fruit, maybe some fun and naughty things with candies or desserts...
That sounds strangely appealing.
Indeed, it is the pinnacle of excess. One of the finer thrills that money well spent can buy.
Did you have any other questions?
Ah! How did things work out for you last time, sir?
Very well. You really know your clubs.
I'm pleased to hear you had a good time.
Nah, I'm good for now.
All right, then. Please do come again!
I'm okay for now, thank you.
Nah, I'm good.

Welcome!
...Ahem! Young miss, what are you doing in a place like this?
